text:
Morgan: quick async standup — what I did / blockers / today
Morgan: what I did: landed a fairness tweak to the slot allocator for microbatches, ran a ~2k-trace kv-eviction sim, and updated perfbench to emit tail-latency histograms
Morgan: blocker: hitting an NPE in the warmup path when prefetch + eviction collide on low-memory GPUs. stack points into prefetch worker -> hidden-state copy
Hannah: can you paste the stack? I saw something similar in prefetch-pr last week and had a potential fix
Morgan: ```
java.lang.NullPointerException at com.redwood.runtime.prefetch.PrefetchWorker.handleSlot(PrefetchWorker.java:241)
 at com.redwood.runtime.kernel.SlotManager.assign(SlotManager.java:134)
```
Hannah: looks like buffer ownership might be getting nulled after eviction. I'll repro locally and try a small patch (likely a missing null-check or late-free)
Jon: queued CR #453 for the allocator changes, added bench output. pinging @Lee for review because of the kernel-level changes
Lee: will review in ~2 hours. heads-up: please add the micro-benchmark CSV to the PR so I can eyeball the distribution, not just p50/p95
Priya: for perfbench runs, can you try a steady 16k-token synthetic workload? previous runs showed slot-steal at p95 under long contexts
Morgan: will run 16k steady and post numbers here in ~20m
perf-bot: benchmark job started: jobs/12345 (perfbench, commit 8a9f7d)
perf-bot: benchmark job succeeded: p50=21ms p95=102ms p99=210ms, mean=28.7ms (16k steady)
Morgan: thanks. improvement vs previous (p95 130ms -> 102ms) but still above our 80ms p95 target for that workload. looks like allocator helps but batcher needs tuning
Hannah: on the kv eviction front, are we set on LRU or should we try frequency-weighted? my read of traces suggests freq-weighted keeps hot keys better for our prefix-heavy traffic
Jon: let's not bikeshed in thread — I'll open a short RFC and tag infra/bench owners, include some trace samples
Lee: small logistics: planning a canary rollout for the allocator+prefetch fix at 4pm PST. need one oncall and one reviewer to watch metrics during rollout
Priya: I can be oncall at 4pm, will also push final quant-profile numbers in 30m for Lee's doc review
Morgan: ack, I'll be available for the rollout and will draft the incident blurb for the all-hands later today (still need to finish root-cause for the warmup NPE)
Jon: also FYI @Morgan please reply to the incident follow-up re: cache-warmup doc — product asked for a short summary by EOD
Morgan: noted, will send a draft by EOD
Hannah: update from me: unblocked on prefetch patch, will open PR once I reproduce the NPE in the small harness
Lee: blocker for me: waiting on micro-bench CSVs to finalize quant-profile docs — Priya said she'll send in 30m
Priya: sending now (uploading to shared bucket), will paste links in CRs
Morgan: thanks everyone :thumbsup: 
Morgan: quick ask — @Lee @Jon if you can prioritize CR review for #453 today that'd help unblock the 4pm canary
Lee: noted, prioritizing it after lunch
Jon: same, will squeeze it in before canary
Morgan: cool — that's it for me. short sync, back to debugging.
